analysis.title: Diplomat Departures Damage Green Day; Kremlin Drives Crude, Credit, & Crypto Crazy
key_insights: Oil ran on headlines all day. Brent rose above $110 and WTI above $101 overnight after UKMTO confirmed at least two more tanker attack incidents in Gulf waters and the Strait of Hormuz area.

Oil peaked around 6am ET and rolled over on reports the Kremlin told Trump envoy Steve Witkoff that Russia is 'in principle, ready to resume' trilateral negotiations. A US general license (131K) related to Russia and a China-Russia agreement to expand oil cooperation added to the decline.

Late in the day oil reversed higher after a report that the US State Department is set to order departure of certain staff and families from US embassies across the Gulf, followed by a report that an Aramco oil field in the Eastern region was attacked. WTI moved back into the green.
Dated Brent (physical barrels) rose again, and diesel fell as the first Russian tanker is on its way to America.
Oil and bond yields tracked each other all day while stocks decoupled until the last hour. The late oil rise pushed yields higher across the curve, with the short end underperforming.
The 20Y Treasury auction tailed, with the highest yield since January 1986. French 10Y yields topped 5.00%. Rate-hike odds were unchanged.
Hyperscaler CDS spreads hit a new record wide, while data-center CDS spreads compressed very modestly and aggregate corporate credit risk improved modestly.
NDX outperformed, bid almost non-stop from the cash open until the last hour, when the embassy departure headline spiked crude and pulled stocks well off highs. RTY fell back into the red.

Overnight, data-center operator NextDC fell sharply but the market shrugged it off, unlike the prior day's reaction to Elice, which rebounded limit up overnight. SMCI supported memory names, which stayed rangebound.
Elon Musk's projections lifted SPCX after the close. SPCX bonds weakened as the scale of capex raised credit risk concerns. CRWV stock was unchanged while its bond yield fell back below 15%.

Goldman traders described activity as very quiet (down 5% vs recent averages) with a balanced buy-sell skew: long-only accounts -7% better for sale (selling defensives to buy cyclicals), hedge funds +3% better to buy, concentrated in Tech and Consumer. The hedge fund short ratio at 61% is the highest seen month to date.
Goldman noted signs of a momentum chase: their High Beta Momentum basket was up sharply and SPCX call volume exceeded 1 million contracts, which they read as retail chasing.
SPX ex-AI was unchanged on the day, Mag7 outperformed the SPX 493, and NeoClouds whipsawed to end up about 3%. AI Power continues to slide, mirroring odds of a Democratic sweep at the midterms.
The dollar rallied late on the oil spike, gold tested down toward $4,100, and bitcoin rose toward $85,000, trading as high-beta tech.

Bloomberg's Michael Ball says Q3 earnings support a rotation into quality: demand is resilient, but higher input and financing costs are squeezing margins. JPMorgan reported card spending up 10% y/y, and Wells Fargo said early-stage delinquencies are historically low.
Margin pressure examples: PepsiCo cut its earnings outlook on a margin miss despite stronger sales, and Delta's fuel bill exceeded guidance by more than $500 million.
RBC research finds higher-quality earnings are being rewarded as leadership broadens away from growth, tech and momentum. Widening spreads are a warning sign for small caps sensitive to refinancing.
Meta reports after the close. It has moved at least 8% the day after each of its last five reports, in both directions, and the last two (and the last two Q3 prints) went the wrong way.

PepsiCo lowered its earnings outlook because margins missed expectations despite stronger sales.

SMCI supported big-tech and memory names overnight.

sector_views.rationale: RBC finds higher-quality earnings are being rewarded as leadership broadens away from growth, tech and momentum. Rising input and financing costs raise the premium on strong operating leverage and low balance-sheet leverage.
Widening spreads are a warning sign because small-cap earnings and balance sheets are more sensitive to refinancing conditions.
Long-only accounts sold defensives to buy cyclicals, and a slowdown in the defensive trade is cited as a reason breadth is not better.

earnings_insights: Meta reports Q3 after the close on 10/22. It has moved at least 8% the day after each of its last five reports, and the last two, including the last two Q3 prints, moved down.
PepsiCo lowered its earnings outlook because margins missed expectations despite stronger sales.
Delta's fuel bill exceeded guidance by more than $500 million while demand and pricing remained strong.
Hasbro beat its own expectations for revenue and profit. GM's results showed consumers holding up 'remarkably well'.
JPMorgan reported debit and credit-card spending up 10% y/y. Wells Fargo said something similar, with early-stage delinquencies historically low.
